back2basics.concept: UN Climate Change Conferences (COP) and Consensus Decision-Making
back2basics.text: The Conference of Parties (COP) is an annual UN meeting where countries negotiate climate action under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change. Decisions require consensus, meaning all parties must agree on the text. This ensures inclusivity but can lead to deadlocks if countries have conflicting interests, especially on sensitive issues like fossil fuel use and climate finance.

2026-11-25-pm-37a12f0de9.deck: COP31 in Turkiye concluded without a consensus climate agreement due to disagreements on fossil fuel phase-out language. This outcome highlights the challenges in global climate negotiations and India's position on balancing climate goals with developmental needs.

body.label: Fossil fuel phase-out disagreement
body.text: The main cause was a standoff over including explicit language on fossil fuel phase-out in the final consensus cover text, with the EU and around 130 countries rejecting the text for lacking this.

body.text: The EU and Panama opposed the cover text, accusing it of greenwashing fossil fuels and weakening previous commitments, while India, China, and Saudi Arabia supported the text to maintain fossil fuel use for economic reasons.

body.label: Consensus requirement

body.label: Scheme overview
body.text: The ₹11,000-crore scheme approved by the Cabinet will run for eight years from FY2026-27 to FY2033-34 to develop indigenous manufacturing capacity in Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE).

body.label: Implementation and timeline
body.text: It includes a two-year gestation period (FY2026-27 to FY2027-28) for setting up manufacturing facilities, a five-year incentive disbursement period (FY2028-29 to FY2032-33), and a final year to settle incentives for incremental sales.

body.label: Scheme components
body.text: The scheme has two components: sales-linked incentives for eligible OEMs and component manufacturers, and a grant of up to ₹375 crore for establishing a dedicated CIE testing facility.

sections.heading: What is the new CIE manufacturing scheme about?

body.label: Market size and import dependence
body.text: India's CIE industry is the world’s third-largest with a market size of ₹97,000 crore in FY2024-25, but about 45% of it depends on imports.

body.label: Growth potential
body.text: Driven by infrastructure and housing growth, the CIE market is projected to more than double to ₹2,28,100 crore by FY2029-30.

body.label: Strategic importance
body.text: The scheme aims to enhance self-reliance by reducing import dependence on key equipment like tunnel boring machines and cranes, especially after recent export controls by China on such machinery.

sections.heading: Why does the CIE scheme matter for India’s economy and manufacturing?

body.label: Sales-linked incentives
body.text: Incentives ranging from 8% to 13% of incremental sales value will be provided over five years to approved OEMs and component manufacturers to boost production.

body.label: Testing facility grant
body.text: A grant of up to ₹375 crore, similar to Viability Gap Funding, will support setting up a state-of-the-art dedicated CIE testing facility in India.

back2basics.concept: National Security and Corporate Governance in Tech
back2basics.text: National security concerns can arise when technology companies operate in sensitive sectors or have leadership linked to foreign entities. Corporate governance involves oversight by a company's board to ensure ethical conduct and compliance with laws. When allegations of espionage or conflicts of interest emerge, governments may intervene to protect national interests, especially in strategic industries like AI chip manufacturing.

back2basics.text: The principle of natural justice requires that a person must be given a fair hearing before any adverse action is taken against them. This includes the right to be informed of allegations and the opportunity to present their case. Courts must provide reasons for their decisions, especially when directing investigations, to prevent arbitrary or unjust actions.

2026-11-25-pm-d865989d30.deck: The Supreme Court set aside the Allahabad High Court's interim orders directing CBI and ED investigations into a disproportionate assets complaint against Rahul Gandhi, emphasizing procedural fairness. This ruling highlights the judiciary's role in safeguarding legal principles and due process in politically sensitive cases.

back2basics.text: Electoral roll revision is the process of updating the list of eligible voters to ensure accuracy and remove duplicates or ineligible entries. Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a focused exercise to clean the electoral rolls comprehensively. The Election Commission of India oversees this process to maintain free and fair elections, but it must balance transparency, accuracy, and federal cooperation.

2026-11-25-pm-ddc08ec00c.deck: Jharkhand Assembly held a special session on November 25, 2026, where the Finance Minister moved a resolution against the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls citing 27% suspicious voters. This issue highlights electoral roll revision challenges and federal concerns over Election Commission functioning, relevant for UPSC exams on electoral reforms and Centre-State relations.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Jharkhand Assembly's resolution against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls:
1. The Finance Minister moved the resolution citing 27% suspicious voters in the electoral rolls.
2. The resolution calls for the immediate removal of the Election Commission of India as a whole.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because the resolution specifically calls for the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner, not the entire Election Commission of India.

body.label: Resolution moved
body.text: Jharkhand Finance Minister Radha Krishna Kishore moved a resolution seeking an immediate halt to the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

body.label: Reason for opposition
body.text: The resolution cited procedural complexities and technical shortcomings in the voter list revision process, with 27% of Jharkhand's 2.21 crore voters deemed suspicious and sent notices.

body.label: Allegation against Election Commission
body.text: The minister alleged that the Election Commission of India was acting as a puppet of the Centre and called for removal of the Chief Election Commissioner to protect the Constitution.

body.label: Next steps
body.text: The Assembly planned to discuss challenges related to SIR and vote on the resolution, which if passed, would be sent to the Centre and other authorities.

body.label: Electoral reforms relevance
body.text: The resolution highlights challenges in electoral roll revision, an important aspect of electoral reforms and democratic governance.

body.label: Centre-State relations
body.text: The dispute reflects tensions in federalism, especially regarding the Election Commission's autonomy and Centre's influence.

body.label: Constitutional governance
body.text: Calls for removal of the Chief Election Commissioner raise issues about constitutional bodies' independence and accountability.
